items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: all the people preceding Jesus Christ, all the — they’re all in hell?

ctx.x: Okay. Because I’m often curious about, well in your case, why does someone born in Cleveland, right, become attracted to the African influence or Brazilian music or where do these things come from? Why are you opened up to those kinds of opportunities?

You know I can trace that back to one phrase when I was studying for my first holy communion and some witch-like nun said, “You know if you’re not Catholic you’re going to hell.” And I thought, oh my God, all the people preceding Jesus Christ, all the — they’re all in hell? And I rejected it right there. And so any — I reject tribalism of any kind. And I think that countries and religions and races and nationalities, those are all tribes. And if we can leave the tribal then we can ascend as a whole. So that’s why…
Well I wanted to go there.
